short: Thick armour and an 88 mm gun, paid for in weight, fuel and broken transmissions.
full:
Henschel's design was rushed into production and into action: the first Tigers of the 502nd Heavy Tank Battalion went forward from Mga, near Leningrad, on 29 August 1942, and three broke down before reaching the enemy. The tank weighed 57 tonnes, carried 100 mm of frontal armour and mounted the 8.8 cm KwK 36, which could destroy most Allied tanks at ranges at which their own guns were useless. Some 1,347 were built before production ended in August 1944.

The cost was mobility and availability. Tigers drank fuel, wore out final drives, and needed narrow transport tracks before they could travel by rail. They were issued to independent heavy battalions rather than spread through the panzer divisions, and their reputation ran ahead of them: Allied crews reported Tigers far more often than they met them. Production gave way to the Tiger II, and surviving Tiger Is fought on in Normandy, Italy and the defence of Germany until 1945.
